mentor.mateo.help.prompt: Which part of EV training would you like me to explain again?
mentor.mateo.help.topic.earning: How do I earn EV points?
mentor.mateo.help.topic.allocating: How do I use stored EV points?
mentor.mateo.help.basics.1: Effort Values, or EVs, are training points for HP, Attack, Defense, Sp. Attack, Sp. Defense, or Speed. Each defeated species awards a particular kind of EV.
mentor.mateo.help.basics.2: PokeAether stores newly earned EV points first. Stored points do not improve a stat until you assign them.
mentor.mateo.help.earning.1: A Pokemon must participate in a victorious battle to receive that opponent's EV reward. Open its Summary and check the EVs tab to see what it has stored.
mentor.mateo.help.earning.2: Give the Pokemon a Macho Brace to double the EV points it earns from battles.
mentor.mateo.help.field.1: Choose a stat and tier with a Field Assistant. Before bonuses, Tier 1 gives 1 EV for ₽500, Tier 2 gives 2 EVs for ₽1,500 after 3 Gym Badges, and Tier 3 gives 3 EVs for ₽3,000 after 6 Gym Badges.
mentor.mateo.help.field.2: Every opponent is level 5 and uses only non-damaging moves. Later tiers use later stages of the same evolution line. These training Pokemon cannot be caught, and the session ends when you leave the field.
mentor.mateo.help.allocating.1: Open Party, select the Pokemon's Summary, and choose the EVs tab. Under Allocated EVs, select the stat you want to raise.
mentor.mateo.help.allocating.2: Choose the final Target EV total with the number field or slider. The preview shows how many stored points it uses. Max selects the highest total currently reachable.
mentor.mateo.help.limits.1: Allocated and Stored EVs for one stat can add up to at most 252. A Pokemon can have at most 510 Allocated EVs across all six stats.
mentor.mateo.help.limits.2: Only Allocated EVs count toward 510, but Stored EVs use the remaining space within that stat's 252 limit. You cannot move Allocated EVs back into storage from the EVs screen.

mentor.bike_seller.help.prompt: What would you like to know about mounts?
mentor.bike_seller.help.topic.selecting: How do I select a mount?

mentor.bike_seller.help.topic.license: How does my Mount License work?
mentor.bike_seller.help.selecting.1: Use the Mounts button in the bottom-right overworld controls. Choose the Land slot, then select Cyclizar.
mentor.bike_seller.help.selecting.2: Your choice is saved. Return to the same menu whenever you want to select another land mount you have unlocked.
mentor.bike_seller.help.riding.1: While outdoors, press your Mount key to mount or dismount your selected land mount. The default key is M.
mentor.bike_seller.help.riding.2: You can view or change that key under Settings, then Controls. Land mounts cannot be used indoors, and your follower returns while you ride.
mentor.bike_seller.help.purpose.1: Land mounts replace the bicycle: they let you travel faster across towns and routes without taking an item out of your Bag.
mentor.bike_seller.help.purpose.2: Land mounts are for solid ground. Surf mounts are selected separately and take over when you travel across water.
mentor.bike_seller.help.license.1: Your Mount License is registered for Kanto. It lets you activate any land mount you own while you are outdoors in this region.
mentor.bike_seller.help.license.2: Each region requires its own registration. Open the Mount License in your Key Items to review the regions registered on it.

mentor.gideon.help.greeting: Every successful catch begins with patience and preparation.
mentor.gideon.help.title: Gideon's Catching Guide
mentor.gideon.help.prompt: What would you like to review?
mentor.gideon.help.topic.finding: How do I find a Pokemon?
mentor.gideon.help.topic.catching: How do I catch a Pokemon?
mentor.gideon.help.topic.odds: How do I improve my catch chance?
mentor.gideon.help.finding.1: Looking for a specific Pokemon? Search for it in your Pokedex and open Locations to check whether and where it can be found in the wild.
mentor.gideon.help.finding.2: Want to know every Pokemon available on your current map? Click the wild Pokemon Radar icon beside the map name, then explore encounter terrain such as tall grass.
mentor.gideon.help.catching.1: During a wild battle, weaken the Pokemon without making it faint. Then open the Bag, choose Poke Balls, and select a ball to throw.
mentor.gideon.help.catching.2: Catching is only available in wild battles. Trainer and practice battles do not allow you to capture the opponent's Pokemon.
mentor.gideon.help.odds.1: A Pokemon is easier to catch at low HP. Sleep and freeze help the most; paralysis, burn, and poison also improve your chance.
mentor.gideon.help.odds.2: A Great Ball is more reliable than a Poke Ball, and an Ultra Ball is stronger still. Carry several in case the first throw fails.
mentor.fishing_guru.help.greeting: A good angler keeps learning from every cast.
mentor.fishing_guru.help.title: Fishing Guru's Lessons
mentor.fishing_guru.help.prompt: Which part of Fishing would you like to review?
mentor.fishing_guru.help.topic.catching: How do I catch my catch?
mentor.fishing_guru.help.starting.1: Select a usable rod from the fishing action in your action bar, then stand beside and face a fishable stretch of water.
mentor.fishing_guru.help.starting.2: Click the rod icon beside you or press {fishing_hotkey} to cast your line.
mentor.fishing_guru.help.starting.3: Wait for the ! to appear, then click it or press {fishing_hotkey} again to reel in the bite.
mentor.fishing_guru.help.starting.4: You can change your Fishing hotkey under Settings > Controls. Different maps and rods have different encounters.
mentor.fishing_guru.help.catching.1: A bite starts a wild battle. Weaken the Pokemon, open your Bag, choose Poke Balls, and throw a ball before it defeats your team.
mentor.fishing_guru.help.catching.2: The lesson only counts once you successfully capture a Pokemon reached through a fishing encounter.
mentor.fishing_guru.help.progression.1: Completing fishing battles earns Fishing XP. Higher Fishing levels unlock new species for each rod and, later, stronger rods.
mentor.fishing_guru.help.progression.2: Good and Super Rods also require regional Gym Badges. Open Skills to inspect your level and upcoming rod unlocks.
mentor.fishing_guru.help.treasure.1: After you defeat or catch a Pokemon from a fishing encounter, you may also find a treasure such as a Pearl, Stardust, or Heart Scale.
mentor.fishing_guru.help.treasure.2: Stronger rods have a better treasure chance and can find rarer prizes. Your Fishing level adds a small bonus, but you can find at most one treasure per encounter.
mentor.rocket_rook.help.greeting: A good thief studies the risk before reaching for the reward.
mentor.rocket_rook.help.title: Rook's Thieving Notes
mentor.rocket_rook.help.prompt: Which part of Thieving do you need explained again?
mentor.rocket_rook.help.topic.risk: How do Wanted and jail work?
mentor.rocket_rook.help.basics.1: Stand directly behind a target while they are facing away, then face them and click the Thieving icon or press {pickpocket_hotkey}.
mentor.rocket_rook.help.basics.2: A successful attempt pays Pokédollars directly into your wallet, grants full Thieving XP, and may add one item to your Bag. Open Skills to inspect Wanted, levels, and daily targets.
mentor.rocket_rook.help.risk.1: Successful theft raises Wanted. A higher Wanted level makes future attempts riskier, while higher Thieving levels reduce detection and Wanted gain.
mentor.rocket_rook.help.risk.2: If caught, you pay a target-based wallet fine, spend ten minutes in Viridian jail, and everyone hears about it. You may wait or pay ₽5,000–₽25,000 bail; public services report players at maximum Wanted.
mentor.rocket_rook.help.targets.1: Each target can be attempted once per UTC day. The Thieving page in Skills shows who is available and when the daily list resets.
mentor.rocket_rook.help.targets.2: Children and elderly targets start at level 1. Civilians unlock at 5, followed by progressively more alert NPC classes such as Bug Catchers, Workers, Hikers, Trainers, Scientists, Ace Trainers, and Veterans.
mentor.rocket_rook.help.progression.1: Every attempt grants Thieving XP: successful attempts grant the full amount, while being caught grants 25%. Harder target classes grant more XP, money, and access to better item tables.
mentor.rocket_rook.help.progression.2: Each higher Thieving level improves cash rewards by 1% and reduces detection and Wanted gain, while milestone levels unlock new target classes. Check Skills to track them.
mentor.karate_master.help.greeting: A steady strike reveals what stone keeps hidden.
mentor.karate_master.help.title: Kenji's Rock Smash Lessons
mentor.karate_master.help.prompt: Which part of Rock Smash would you like to review?
mentor.karate_master.help.topic.basics: How do I smash a rock?
mentor.karate_master.help.basics.1: Teach Rock Smash to a compatible Pokemon, stand beside a training rock, face it, and interact. A Rock Smash Charm can also provide the field move.
mentor.karate_master.help.basics.2: You do not need a Gym Badge to use Rock Smash outside battle. Every successful smash grants Rock Smash XP and Pokédollars; the amount grows with the rock's requirement and your Rock Smash level.
mentor.karate_master.help.daily.1: Each fixed rock can be smashed once per UTC day. It returns at the daily reset at 00:00 UTC.
mentor.karate_master.help.daily.2: Open Rock Smash under Skills and choose Rocks to see which locations are still available today.
mentor.karate_master.help.treasure.1: Regular treasures such as Pearls, Stardust, Hard Stones, and Nuggets have a 30% chance to appear. They are a bonus, not a guaranteed drop.
mentor.karate_master.help.treasure.2: Higher-level rocks have larger Pokédollar rewards and can roll Big Pearls, Star Pieces, Big Nuggets, and Comet Shards. Items go directly into your Bag.
mentor.karate_master.help.fossils.1: Complete fossils can appear as a bonus from Rock Smash level 20 onward. You never need to collect fossil fragments.
mentor.karate_master.help.fossils.2: Helix and Dome Fossils are available first. Old Amber joins the fossil table at level 50; your current chance is shown under Skills.

npc.aether_clash_guide.intro: Welcome to Aether Clash. Ask me anything about the arena, its battles, or its formats.
npc.aether_clash_guide.menu.title: Aether Clash Guide
npc.aether_clash_guide.menu.prompt: What would you like to know?
npc.aether_clash_guide.guild_duel.title: Guild Duel
npc.aether_clash_guide.guild_duel.prompt: Two Guilds enter. Which part should I explain?
npc.aether_clash_guide.battle_royale.pro: This format is still being prepared. What would you like to know?
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.overview.1: Aether Clash is a Guild competition fought across a shared arena.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.overview.2: Win PvP battles and keep at least one Guild member active. The last Guild with active Trainers wins.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.battle_flo: Touch an enemy Trainer's clash ring to start a PvP battle.
The loser is eliminated and sent to jail. The winner returns to the arena.
A rotating Master Ball marks Trainers who are battling, so spectators can select it to watch.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.rules.1: Each Clash uses the battle tier selected in its challenge. Tier rules and bans come from the same ruleset used by Ranked.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.rules.2: Clash battles use their own fixed timers. Check your party with Ranked Team Validation before entering.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.rules.3: A stake is held from each Guild Bank. The winner receives the entire pot, so both Guilds must have enough funds.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.timers.1: Guild Duel uses separate clocks: challenges expire after 60 seconds, accepted Guilds have 2 minutes to enter, and each free active Trainer gets 60 seconds to find a battle before automatic matchmaking.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.timers.2: Inside a battle, Team Preview allows 15 seconds, each move choice up to 20 seconds, and a forced switch 10 seconds. Move choices draw from your 60-second personal bank, which restores 5 seconds when each new move turn opens.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.timers.3: If a move-choice timer runs out, that Trainer forfeits the battle. Team Preview and forced-switch timeouts choose the first available legal option instead.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.timers.4: After Team Preview, a separate 7-minute-30-second battle limit appears in the header and Damage Calculator and keeps running through disconnects. At zero, most remaining Pokemon wins, then most hidden damage dealt; an exact tie eliminates both Trainers.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.joining.1: During the entry window, participating members enter their format's lobby portal. The roster locks when the countdown ends.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.joining.2: Late arrivals and permitted visitors enter as spectators in jail. Spectator access depends on the challenge or event settings.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.joining.3: Use an Aether View orb to explore and Master Balls to watch battles. Arena portals let you leave.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.guild_duel: Only Guild Leaders and Captains can send or accept a Guild Duel challenge. Challenge an opposing Leader or Captain through their player menu.
An unanswered challenge expires after 60 seconds. A Guild can only have one accepted or running Clash at a time.
After a challenge is accepted, Guild members have two minutes to enter the red Guild Duel portal.
Team sizes do not need to match. Whoever is inside when the portal closes becomes the locked roster.
If one Guild brings nobody, the other wins by no-show. If both stay away, the Clash ends without a winner.
The duel continues until one Guild has no active players left. The surviving Guild wins.
Enemy names stay hidden in the arena and are revealed only in battle. Share any identities you discover with your Guild.
A free active Trainer gets 60 seconds to find a battle in the arena.
When the timer expires, the Clash pairs available opponents automatically. If nobody is free, it waits until an opponent becomes available.
npc.aether_clash_guide.answer.battle_roy: Battle Royale will bring several Guilds into one arena during scheduled events.
It uses the same battle and elimination flow as Guild Duel, with one shared jail for eliminated Trainers.
The purple lobby portal is reserved for Battle Royale and is not open yet.
When events become available, enter before the event countdown ends. The roster will then lock for the event.
Guilds are eliminated one by one when they run out of active Trainers.
The last Guild with an active Trainer becomes the Battle Royale winner.
